XAdES-BES signing for MyInvois document version 1.1, and the two layers it
needed — Canonical XML 1.1 in the core, and the UBL signature components OASIS
ships but this package had never modelled.

Additive: nothing was removed from the public API and no import path moved, so
an application on 0.2.0 compiles unchanged.

## Signing

```ts
const signing = myInvois.withSigner({ sign, certificate });
signing.defaults(invoice);
await signing.finalize(invoice);   // bumps listVersionID to 1.1, then signs
```

The private key never enters the library — `sign` is a callback, so a file, a
smartcard, an HSM or a cloud KMS all work, and the package still runs in a
browser. `certificate.issuerName` is supplied rather than parsed: the order of
the relative names is not canonical and differs between CAs.

Version 1.0 is unchanged and remains the default.

## Verified against LHDN's own signed document

`test/fixtures/lhdn/one-doc-signed.xml` is a signed invoice published by LHDN,
carrying real digests and a signature from Pos Digicert's "Trial LHDNM Sub CA
V1". Measured against it, offline, with no certificate or credentials:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| DocDigest | reproduces exactly — canonicalization **and** the transform |
| CertDigest | reproduces exactly |
| SignatureValue | verifies — the signature covers the document, not `ds:SignedInfo` |
| PropsDigest | **does not reproduce**, from anything |

That last row is recorded rather than hidden. Sixteen candidate serialisations
were tried, then 133,467 substrings of the file under three normalisations.
Nothing matches — a different finding from "we compute it wrong", since the
other three reproduce. Nothing binds that digest cryptographically here, so a
stale value in the sample would never have been noticed. If a real submission
returns `DS320`, `digestedProperties` in `profiles/myinvois/sign.ts` carries
the one-line alternative and the evidence on both sides.

The exercise also settled a contradiction: the sample declares
`Algorithm="…xml-exc-c14n#"` and is wrong about its own content — exclusive
c14n yields a different digest, and the published value is the non-exclusive
one.

**No submission has yet been accepted.** Treat 1.1 as unverified against the
live service; LHDN's preprod currently returns `SystemError` for individual
(`IG`-prefix) taxpayers, which is an upstream defect rather than a client one.

## Canonical XML 1.1

`toXmlString(node, { canonical: true })`. No new dependency and still
browser-safe: Node has no canonicalizer and the ones on npm are Node-only, so
this is written directly from the node tree. c14n11 is deliberately
non-exclusive — it keeps the `xmlns:ext` declaration that the transform leaves
unused, which is what LHDN assumes when it verifies.

A new `check:c14n` gate asserts the property that matters —
`c14n11(the bytes we submit) == the bytes we digest` — with xmllint standing in
for LHDN's processor.

## `sig:` and `sac:` components

`@weiliang79/ubl-builder/sig` adds `UBLDocumentSignatures`,
`SignatureInformation` and `SignatureExtensionContent`.

## One behaviour change

Empty attributes are no longer dropped. Both writers used to filter on
truthiness, so an attribute set to `''` vanished — as did a legitimate `0` or
`false`. XMLDSig's first `ds:Reference` carries `URI=""`, which means "this
whole document" and is not the same claim as omitting it.

Affects only code that deliberately sets an attribute to `''`, `0` or `false`.
No fixture changed, and the golden MyInvois invoice still serialises to the
same 4542 bytes.

## Certificates

Signing needs an **organisational** certificate from an MCMC-licensed CA. Self-
signed certificates are rejected in the sandbox as well as in production
(`DS329`), and `X509IssuerName` must be RFC 4514 order — the reverse of
OpenSSL's rendering — or submissions return `DS326`.

See [MIGRATION.md](./MIGRATION.md#migrating-to-030).
